voice_text: Plants are special living things because they can make their own food. This process is called photosynthesis, and it happens mostly in the green leaves.
visual_instruction: A green leaf in sunlight with the title Photosynthesis

voice_text: To make food, a plant needs three things: sunlight, water from the soil, and carbon dioxide from the air.
visual_instruction: A plant with three arrows pointing to the leaf

voice_text: Leaves are green because of chlorophyll. Chlorophyll captures the energy of sunlight so the leaf can turn raw materials into food.
visual_instruction: A leaf cell zoomed in to show chloroplasts

voice_text: During photosynthesis the plant makes a sugar called glucose. The plant uses glucose for energy and stores the extra as starch.
subtitle_text: Plants make glucose and store starch.
visual_instruction: Glucose molecule and a potato storing starch

voice_text: To remember: plants take in sunlight, water and carbon dioxide, and make glucose and oxygen. The oxygen goes out into the air for us to breathe.
subtitle_text: Plants give us food and oxygen.
